verifications.claim: NASA's Artemis II mission successfully launched on April 1, 2026, at 6:35 p.m. EDT from Kennedy Space Center in Florida.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: '6:36 PM / April 1, 2026 Artemis II lifts off Artemis II lifted off at 6:35 p.m. EDT.' 'The Artemis II mission is launching from the Kennedy Space Center in Florida'; R3: 'lifted off from Kennedy Space Center’s Launch Complex 39B in Florida at 6:35 p.m. EDT'; R5: 'Artemis II lifted off at 6:35 p.m. EDT.'
verifications.reasoning: Exact date, time, location, and success confirmed directly in multiple sources.

verifications.claim: The Space Launch System (SLS) rocket lifted off.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'NASA's Artemis II SLS (Space Launch System) rocket'; R3: 'NASA’s Artemis II SLS (Space Launch System) rocket... lifted off'; R5: 'Artemis II lifts off'; R7: 'NASA’s historic Artemis II mission to the moon launched... Space Launch System rocket'.
verifications.reasoning: All sources confirm SLS rocket lifted off for Artemis II.

verifications.claim: The SLS rocket sent astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen on a 10-day journey around the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'astronauts — commander Reid Wiseman, pilot Victor Glover, mission specialist Christina Koch and Canadian astronaut Jeremy Hansen'; R3: 'NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, and Christina Koch, along with CSA (Canadian Space Agency) astronaut Jeremy Hansen'; multiple: '10-day mission around the Moon'.
verifications.reasoning: Exact crew names and 10-day lunar mission confirmed.

verifications.claim: Artemis II marks the first crewed lunar mission in over 50 years.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'first piloted moonshot since the end of the Apollo program 53 years ago'; R3: 'The approximately 10-day Artemis II mission around the Moon is the first crewed flight under NASA’s Artemis campaign.'
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly state first crewed lunar mission since Apollo (over 50 years).

verifications.claim: The crew is safely in orbit.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: '7:54 AM / April 2, 2026 Artemis II crew begins first day in space after exhilarating launch'; R5: 'NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman has... well and safely in orbit.'
verifications.reasoning: Post-launch updates confirm crew safe in orbit.

verifications.claim: There was a minor reported issue with the Orion capsule's toilet system.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: '8:33 PM / April 1, 2026 Issue with toilet being worked on The crew is dealing with a "controller issue" with the toilet'; R2: 'There was a little potty problem on NASA's Artemis 2 moon ship... glitch in... toilet'.
verifications.reasoning: Direct reports of minor toilet/controller issue post-launch.

verifications.claim: The 10-day mission is the first crewed flight beyond low Earth orbit since 1972.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'higher than any astronauts have flown since the final Apollo moon mission in 1972'; R3: 'first crewed deep-space flight in over 50 years'.
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm first crewed beyond LEO since 1972, 10-day mission.

verifications.claim: The mission is testing critical systems for future lunar landings.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'thoroughly test their Orion capsule... to make sure it's up to the task'; R3: 'test the systems and hardware needed to continue sending astronauts on increasingly difficult missions'.
verifications.reasoning: Explicitly described as test mission for Orion systems for future missions.

verifications.claim: The SLS rocket produced 8.8 million pounds of force.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'launches with 8.8 million pounds of thrust'; R3: 'generated an incredible 8.8 million pounds of force at liftoff'.
verifications.reasoning: Exact thrust figure for SLS confirmed.

verifications.claim: The launch had a 90% "go" rating for favorable weather.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'NASA said the weather was 90% go for launch'; R3: 'The weather continues to cooperate and has now been upgraded to 90% go for launch'.

verifications.claim: The crew includes NASA astronaut Reid Wiseman (commander).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'commander Reid Wiseman'; R3: 'NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman, commander'.

verifications.claim: The crew includes NASA astronaut Victor Glover (pilot).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'pilot Victor Glover'; R3: 'Victor Glover, pilot'.

verifications.claim: The crew includes NASA astronaut Christina Koch (mission specialist).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'mission specialist Christina Koch'; R3: 'Christina Koch, mission specialist'.

verifications.claim: The crew includes CSA astronaut Jeremy Hansen (mission specialist).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Canadian astronaut Jeremy Hansen'; R3: 'CSA (Canadian Space Agency) astronaut Jeremy Hansen, mission specialist'.

verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R1: Multiple holds and issues resolved ('NO-GO' due to FTS, battery issue, but unanimous 'go' poll); R3: Holds at T-10, issues resolved but proceeded.
verifications.reasoning: Countdown had holds and minor issues resolved, but ultimately successful; not entirely 'smooth' but no major scrubs.

verifications.claim: The mission successfully began the next phase of the Artemis program.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'test flight... opening act in a series of missions'; R3: 'first crewed flight under NASA’s Artemis campaign... paving the way for future lunar landings'.
verifications.reasoning: Launch success initiates crewed phase of Artemis program.
